edges.description: Storage develops, but not in the tissue compartment that defines the human disease.
edges.limitations: Neither this line nor the alpha/beta line develops the cytoplasmic vacuolar inclusions in fibrocytes and mesenchymal cells - the I-cells - that characterise the skeletal and connective-tissue disease in human ML II and ML III. The predominant murine lesion is in exocrine secretory epithelium instead, which is not where the human disease is felt. This line is also reported to lack cartilage defects outright, which a second gamma-null line contradicts; see the cartilage controversy recorded in this entry. Storage-burden or connective-tissue endpoints should not be transferred from this model to patients.

edges.description: Substrate accumulates inside chondrocytes and the cartilage matrix is altered, which is the connective-tissue storage this node names.
edges.limitations: Chondrocytes and tendon were assayed; the I-cell inclusions in fibrocytes and mesenchymal cells that define the human lesion were not reported here and were absent in the Lexicon line. The Lexicon line is reported to lack cartilage defects altogether, so this readout is contradicted by the other gamma-null model in this entry.

edges.description: A functional joint deficit that the authors attribute to fatigue or pain at the joint, which is the closest available model correlate of the chronic joint pain reported by patients.
edges.limitations: Rotarod performance under fatigue is a composite motor readout, not a pain measurement. The authors offer fatigue or pain as alternative explanations and do not separate them, and no nociceptive assay was performed, so this link rests on the authors' interpretation rather than on a direct measure of pain.

nodes.description: A second, independently derived gamma-subunit null line, curated separately from the Lexicon line above because it is a different mouse. The reporting paper's Animals section states that its Gnptg ko (C57Bl/6) mice "have been described previously (Kollmann et al., 2012, 2013; Di Lorenzo et al., 2018)", a provenance distinct from the Lexicon allele. It is the line in which the cartilage and joint phenotype was found.

Knockout of the GlcNAc-1-phosphotransferase gamma subunit, studied alongside the alpha/beta-subunit knockout that models mucolipidosis II. The pairing is what makes this model informative: losing the gamma subunit causes only a partial loss of mannose-6-phosphate tagging, where losing alpha/beta abolishes it, and the severity of storage disease in the two lines tracks the residual enzyme activity. That graded relationship is the mouse counterpart of the milder human ML III gamma against ML II.
Progressive joint stiffness and restriction of movement.
